title: Code dictation — Build Order
rule: Say code the way you would say it to a person, and get code that runs — no training the speaker; the rules learn the phrasing people actually use.

stages.name: Python by voice
stages.does: A third hotkey turns speech into Python: keywords, operators, strings, brackets that close themselves, block colons, and a 5,965-name table from numpy, pandas, matplotlib, seaborn, scikit-learn, scipy and torch.
stages.see: "for i in range len numbers" types for i in range(len(numbers)):
stages.proof: Grade from a mark dictated by Omar into Trace Table passed its tests (15 Sep) after six live rounds (decision 10).

items.t: Live: Grade from a mark passed

stages.name: Library script, scored
stages.does: Scores the 22-line pandas/numpy/matplotlib script dictated in Omar's own words, and fixes what rules can.
stages.see: A data script dictated in one press runs.
stages.proof: Replay of the second run: 20 of 22 lines as meant (the 2 misses are real words: buy/by, hi/high). A fresh third dictation should reach 20 of 22.

needs.label: Omar's third dictation of the script

stages.name: Cambridge pseudocode
stages.does: The same engine for IGCSE 0478 / A Level 9618 pseudocode: DECLARE, ←, IF … THEN … ENDIF, CASE OF, FOR … NEXT, OUTPUT/INPUT, uppercase keywords.
stages.see: "case of mark" types CASE OF Mark with the right indentation and ENDCASE.
stages.proof: A Trace Table pseudocode question passes from a single dictation. 491 tests pass; **not yet dictated live.**

stages.name: SQL
stages.does: SQL by voice: uppercase keywords, snake_case names, quoted strings, a closing semicolon.
stages.see: "select star from students where age greater than 16" types SELECT * FROM students WHERE age > 16;
stages.proof: A query dictated into Trace Table's SQL track runs. 522 tests pass; **not yet dictated live.**

stages.name: TypeScript
stages.does: TypeScript by voice: camelCase names, const/let, ===, arrow functions, braces and semicolons.
stages.see: "const user name equals quote Omar" types const userName = "Omar";
stages.proof: A TypeScript file dictated into VS Code compiles. 522 tests pass; **not yet dictated live.**
